subtopic: General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)
stem:
For \(\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}\) and \(\text{M}^{3+}/\text{M}^{2+}\) systems the \(E^{\circ}\) values for some metals are as follows:

| Couple | \(E^{\circ}\) |
|---|---|
| \(\text{Cr}^{2+}/\text{Cr}\) | \(-0.9\,\text{V}\) |
| \(\text{Mn}^{2+}/\text{Mn}\) | \(-1.2\,\text{V}\) |
| \(\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe}\) | \(-0.4\,\text{V}\) |
| \(\text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}^{2+}\) | \(-0.4\,\text{V}\) |
| \(\text{Mn}^{3+}/\text{Mn}^{2+}\) | \(+1.5\,\text{V}\) |
| \(\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}\) | \(+0.8\,\text{V}\) |

Use this data to comment upon:

(i) the stability of \(\text{Fe}^{3+}\) in acid solution as compared to that of \(\text{Cr}^{3+}\) or \(\text{Mn}^{3+}\) and

(ii) the ease with which iron can be oxidised as compared to a similar process for either chromium or manganese metal.
